userStories.title: Drawing a table grid
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement `renderTable`'s fitting-grid branch with terminal-column sizing, muted borders, bold headers, markdown alignment and wrapped styled cells.

**Motivation** — `layout.ts` then wraps those source lines when they are wider than the column, which breaks the pipes across lines.

**Approach** — **Grid geometry.** For `n` columns with content widths `w1..wn`, every grid line is `sum(w) + 3n + 1` columns wide: a vertical glyph, then per column a space, the cell content padded to `wi`, a space and a vertical glyph. Lines, top to bottom: a top border (`topLeft`, `horizontal` repeated `wi + 2` per column joined by `topJoin`, `topRight`), the header row(s), a separator (`midLeft`, `midJoin`, `midRight`) when there is at least one body row, the body rows with no separator between them, and a bottom border (`bottomLeft`, `bottomJoin`, `bottomRight`). Border and vertical glyphs are `muted`; header cell spans are bold on top of their own styles; padding spaces are unstyled.

**Column sizing (`columnWidths`).** The natural width of a column is the widest cell in it (header included), measured in terminal columns with `spansWidth`, and at least 1. The budget is `width - (3n + 1)`. If the natural widths fit the budget they are used. Otherwise each column's floor is `min(natural, MIN_CELL_WIDTH)` with `MIN_CELL_WIDTH = 3`; if the floors do not fit the budget, `columnWidths` returns `undefined` (stack). Otherwise it shrinks one column by one column-width at a time, always the currently widest column above its floor (on a tie, the leftmost), until the widths sum to the budget. Example: natural `[10, 4, 20]` with budget 20 gives `[8, 4, 8]`.

**Cells.** Each cell is wrapped to its column width with `wrap` from `wrap.ts` (word wrap, a word longer than the column breaks between grapheme clusters), an empty cell is one blank line, and a row is as tall as its tallest cell; shorter cells are padded with blank lines below. Each cell line, header cells included, is padded to the column width by its column's alignment: `left` and `null` pad on the right, `right` pads on the left, `center` puts `floor(extra / 2)` spaces on the left and the rest on the right. A row with fewer cells than the header draws the missing cells empty; cells beyond the header count are not drawn.

Patterns to mirror: `codeBlockLines` and `ruleLine` in `markdown.ts` (muted frame glyphs from `context.theme.glyphs`, `mergeSpans`/`styled` construction), `_markdownDeps` as the injected seam (`markdown.test.ts` already swaps `highlight`). Module rules: `src/tui/chat/` sibling imports are relative (`./wrap`), `markdown-table.ts` is not added to the `src/tui/chat/index.ts` barrel (it has no consumer outside the directory), new source stays under the 600-line gate.

**Scope** — In: extend the upstream-created `markdown-table.ts` and its tests; derive natural widths from model cells, use `columnWidths` to choose the branch, draw Unicode/ASCII grids, handle empty headers, header-only tables, wrapped/ragged rows and existing inline styles. Out: when `columnWidths` returns `undefined`, this story's `renderTable` may return any lines; US-003 defines them. Theme and sizing API changes belong to US-001; actual markdown dispatch and layout test replacement belong to US-004. Separator lines between body rows of the grid. Adding any package dependency for table rendering; the renderer is built on `marked`'s existing table token and `wrap.ts`. Changing the fence glyphs (`codeTop`, `codeSide`, `codeBottom`) or sharing them with the table glyph set. Exporting `markdown-table.ts` from the `src/tui/chat/index.ts` barrel; it has no consumer outside `src/tui/chat/`. `markdown-table.ts` importing `markdown.ts`; cells arrive as styled spans so the dependency runs one way only.

**Interface** — Use the upstream `TableModel`, `RenderTableOptions`, `TableAlign` and `MIN_CELL_WIDTH` unchanged.
```ts
/** Content width per column for `width`, or undefined when the floors do not fit (stack). */
export function columnWidths(natural: readonly number[], width: number): readonly number[] | undefined;

/** The grid when the columns fit, otherwise the stacked layout. */
export function renderTable(model: TableModel, options: RenderTableOptions): StyledLine[];
```
The stacked branch of the final renderer contract is completed by US-003. Existing helpers, read only:
```ts
wrap(spans: readonly Span[], width: number, prefix?: readonly Span[]): StyledLine[]
spansWidth(spans: readonly Span[]): number
mergeSpans(spans: readonly Span[]): StyledLine
styled(text: string, style: SpanStyle): Span
type SpanStyle = Omit<Span, "text">
```

analysis:
This is an enhancement to the existing @nathapp/nax Bun/TypeScript React/Ink chat renderer, not a greenfield project. Codebase-memory MCP tools are not exposed in this session, so structural discovery used the available direct file reads and text searches instead. No code or tests were executed while drafting this PRD. The supplied baseline commit is a locator only; implementation must read the current files before editing.

Goal and completion: render marked table tokens in assistant replies as a full muted box grid with bold headers, preserved inline styles, markdown alignment, deterministic widest-first shrinking and wrapped cells; switch to stacked Header: value blocks only when column floors cannot fit. Every table line must fit its own block's content budget, not the outer terminal width. Binding implementation sequence is exactly US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 -> US-004, all scoped to packages/nax. No dependency, release, configuration, persisted transcript, or public barrel migration is required.

Existing architecture and data flow: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/markdown.ts:26 imports marked; packages/nax/package.json:95 pins marked 18.1.0. renderMarkdown at markdown.ts:273 resolves the caller's width, lexes the document, catches lexer failures into sanitized source lines, and inserts one blank line between nonempty top-level blocks. blockLines at markdown.ts:243 dispatches supported block tokens; tables currently reach the sourceLines fallback at markdown.ts:263. _markdownDeps at markdown.ts:67 currently contains only highlight. inlineSpans at markdown.ts:154 recursively styles cell-compatible inline tokens; inlineToken at markdown.ts:124 applies bold/emphasis/accent and sanitized text via singleLine at markdown.ts:92. baseStyle at markdown.ts:114 carries italic from quotes. The new table dispatch must use inlineSpans(cell.tokens, baseStyle(context)) for both header and body cells, copy align, and call the actual injected _markdownDeps.renderTable seam, not a direct renderer call that bypasses the spy. The marked Table token normalization (short rows padded, extra cells discarded) is supplied by the spec; the pure renderer must still normalize directly supplied ragged TableModel rows by header count.

Width ownership: itemBlockLines at markdown.ts:171 subtracts the bounded list prefix from the context width before rendering a child, and blockquoteLines at markdown.ts:206 subtracts the quote prefix and sets italic:true. Neither mechanism should change. ruleLine at markdown.ts:217 and codeBlockLines at markdown.ts:230 show the existing muted frame and mergeSpans/styled patterns to mirror. layout.ts:138 replyLines calls renderMarkdown with width=context.width-GUTTER_WIDTH, minWidth=MIN_REPLY_WIDTH and cutCode:true, then prefixes the bullet on the first line and the blank gutter thereafter. The fallback prefixedLine at packages/nax/src/tui/chat/layout-lines.ts:206 wraps an over-wide result. Tables must fit before that fallback is reached; do not modify layout runtime behavior or remove wrapping for raw HTML/other fallbacks. At terminal width 20 the reply budget is 18, and a four-column table with the specified long headers must stack. At width 17 four natural one-column cells fit a grid; at width 16 they must stack. These boundary cases establish that renderTable really uses columnWidths. Update only stale table-source references in the markdown.ts header/default comments, layout.ts header/replyLines comments, and wrap.ts wrapSpans comment.

Theme impact: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/theme.ts:33 defines ChatGlyphs, theme.ts:143 and theme.ts:161 define its Unicode and ASCII objects, theme.ts:236 chooses by NAX_ASCII/locale, and theme.ts:247 resolves the full theme. Add an exported TableGlyphs interface and a readonly table member to both complete glyph objects without changing existing fence glyphs or color/locale resolution. Theme consumers include ChatApp.tsx:57, styled-line.tsx:14, layout.ts:63, layout-status.ts:18, chat-status.ts:17, and the public index.ts:10. layout-status.ts:32 uses a literal status map constrained with keyof ChatGlyphs; its actual keys remain notice/warning/error and require no behavioral change. Text search found no handwritten ChatGlyphs or glyphs-object literals in packages/nax/test; existing tests obtain themes through resolveChatTheme. The new nested glyph object is additive, but watch any exact whole-theme snapshots or custom structural fixtures encountered during implementation. Do not export markdown-table.ts from index.ts.

New pure leaf module: create only packages/nax/src/tui/chat/markdown-table.ts and packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/markdown-table.test.ts in US-001. The renderer takes immutable, already-styled spans and TableGlyphs, never imports markdown.ts, and has no I/O or new dependency. Use relative sibling imports and keep the supplied names and signatures unchanged. US-001 establishes theme, types, MIN_CELL_WIDTH=3 and columnWidths; US-002 adds grid renderTable and computes natural widths from the header and header-count body cells; US-003 completes its stacked fallback and width floor; US-004 wires it into markdown replies. Types created by US-001 can be context for all later stories, but only US-001 lists those files as expectedFiles.

Span/width primitives: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/styled-line.tsx:17 defines Span, :26 defines readonly StyledLine, :29 fixes MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH=10, :41 exposes plainText, :46 measures with Bun.stringWidth, and :71 sanitizes with Bun.stripANSI plus control stripping. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/wrap.ts:53 provides resolveWidth; :59 styled; :74 mergeSpans; :88 spansWidth; :126 segments combined text across style boundaries; :160 groups words and drops trailing separators; :196 implements oversized-cluster fallback; :307 wraps directly to the requested content width; :340 wrapSpans applies the outer layout floor. Use wrap, not wrapSpans, for narrow cells and stacked content. wrap([]) returns no lines, so grid empty cells need an explicit blank line and shorter cells need bottom fill. Preserve all input styles when adding header bold; leave synthetic padding and colon/separator text unstyled. mergeSpans can merge adjacent plain runs, so assertions should inspect styled text runs without depending on every unstyled padding fragment retaining its own span identity. Natural widths are terminal columns with minimum 1, not JavaScript string length.

Risks and edge cases: shrinking must select the currently widest column above its individual min(natural,3) floor and prefer the leftmost tie, with frame overhead 3n+1. Ignore extra row cells even when measuring natural widths; otherwise hidden data could shrink or stack a visible table. Header-only grids omit the middle rule, empty headers return [], centered odd padding places the extra space on the right, and wrapped header lines remain aligned and bold. Stacked empty labels omit the colon, empty values retain a bare colon after a nonempty label, and entirely empty rows must not introduce empty blocks or adjacent rules. Header-only stacked tables render bold headers without labels/colons. Width below 1 must behave like 1, not the general layout minimum of 10. Existing wrap's splitGlyph fallback cannot make a single double-column code point fit a one-column budget; normal reply content budgets and grid floors avoid that case, but direct renderTable widths near 1 merit careful review rather than assuming the helper proves every possible width invariant. This PRD does not authorize a broad rewrite of shared wrapping. One-step widest-first shrinking is deterministic but can do many iterations for extremely long cells; preserve the specified algorithm/leftmost tie semantics. Streaming input must remain a paragraph until marked emits a table token. Cell sanitization must remain upstream through inlineSpans, including screen-control escapes; this is preservation of an existing text-rendering boundary, not an authentication/session/permission change.

Tests and migration: packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/theme.test.ts:175 exercises glyph resolution and :246 pins glyph/color independence; extend it with the exact nested table sets. markdown.test.ts:301 currently expects source-table lines and must be replaced with the exact five-line grid expectation; the neighboring raw HTML fallback at :305 stays unchanged. Its highlighter seam cleanup at :464 is scoped to the highlighting fallback describe; table spies need their own covering afterEach or an appropriately broadened cleanup, always restoring the original function even after a failing test. layout.test.ts:298 covers replies and :354 currently checks squashed table source; replace that assertion with bounded stacked header output, keeping the unrelated HTML and fence behavior unchanged. Add the two layoutTranscript integration assertions there; they exercise the real markdown renderer rather than a layout stub. Existing wrap.test.ts:28 and :40 pin style-preserving wrapping, and markdown.test.ts:237 onward covers graphemes/prefix budgets. Table-specific unit tests should assert exact plain texts, span styles, and spansWidth for double-width text and wrapping, using the real theme and shared primitives. Use bun:test and the _deps seam instead of global module mocking. Targeted commands, if needed outside automatic execution, are run from packages/nax, e.g. bun test test/unit/tui/chat/markdown-table.test.ts --timeout=30000 and the affected theme/markdown/layout test paths. Never run bare bun test or bun run nax; the pipeline supplies lint/typecheck/tests, and coverage must not be run inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1.

Conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:13 links conventions and :24 links function/testing standards; its quick reference sets a 600-line source hard limit and 800-line test hard limit. Existing markdown.test.ts has 521 lines and layout.test.ts 686, so keep new cases concise and within the test file limit. No generated AGENTS.md/CLAUDE rules should be edited. outOfScope: Copying a rendered table back out as markdown source: the transcript holds the drawn grid, and a terminal selection copies the box glyphs.
Horizontal scrolling or a "show source" toggle for wide tables; the wrap-then-stack rule is the only answer to width.
Separator lines between body rows of the grid.

Tables in thinking blocks, user messages, tool results or listings; only replies go through `renderMarkdown`.
Changing the fence glyphs (`codeTop`, `codeSide`, `codeBottom`) or sharing them with the table glyph set.
A configurable `MIN_CELL_WIDTH`, column-width hints, or a per-table style choice.
Adding any package dependency for table rendering; the renderer is built on `marked`'s existing table token and `wrap.ts`.
Exporting `markdown-table.ts` from the `src/tui/chat/index.ts` barrel; it has no consumer outside `src/tui/chat/`.
